meta.summary: A 2.5-minute app walkthrough: one presenter in a warm, dim living-room set, cut against bright full-screen phone recordings on a pale blue gradient, tab by tab, ending on a black end card.

acts.name: Status and permissions

acts.name: Feed
acts.function: Personalised feed and its editable prompt.

acts.name: Ideas
acts.function: Proactive suggestions list, read in a slow zoomed scroll.

acts.name: Goals
acts.function: Goals with lightweight status, a detail timeline, long-term goals.

acts.name: Library
acts.function: Everything the agent made; opens an interactive dashboard artifact.

acts.name: Sign-off and end card
acts.function: Thanks, call to download, black end card with icon, store badges, Meta.

voice_track.words: Hey, my name is {PRESENTER_NAME} and I'm very excited to give you a quick walkthrough of our new app, Muse.
Your personal agent who's always working for you.
And we'll start out on the chat tab, where you'll notice it feels very similar to a messaging app, and that is intentional.
Speaking with AI usually
begins with a blank screen, and we wanted this to feel more like
a conversation between you and your very capable personal agent,
Muse, who you can see at the top of the screen.
Now, I talk to mine about all kinds of topics, it's usually golf,
but I also have it do things for me, like buy movie tickets,
help me plan a very complex weekend away with my family,
or I have given it access to my chess account so it can monitor my very frequent losses
and send me an analysis in the morning.
And it can do all these things because it has its own computer and it's always working in the background.
So it's useful for me to see what it's doing at any given time,
and I can see that at the status display in the top of the screen.
If I want more detail, I can tap on it and I'll see what it's doing, what it has done, what it will do,
and if any of these actions require my permission, I can grant that here or in chat.
The next tab is the feed,
and this is where Muse will find content for you that it thinks you'll find interesting.
And you can help define what that is using the prompt in the top of the screen.
And you can be very specific.
So if you want to see finance news in the morning and non-fiction book recommendations in the evening, you can do that.
Each one of these posts will be written just for you.
The next tab is
ideas, and this is where I'll find a list of proactive suggestions from my Muse based on our conversations.
So I'll see a list of things like lower back recovery regimen, kindergarten coordination, permit applications,
lots of different examples of ways that Muse thinks it can help me better.
And
ultimately, Muse is designed to help you accomplish
your goals, and you'll find them here on the goals tab.
These will appear based on your conversation with Muse; as it learns what you care about, you'll see them appear.
And you can see a lightweight status based on what Muse has been doing in the background.
You can also tap for more detail and a full timeline.
And if there are things that you want to tackle on a longer timeline, you can do that as well, down below.
Now, anything
you create with Muse, you can find on
the library tab.
Simple documents, PDFs, Markdown files, but also really rich and interactive artifacts, like my chess analysis dashboard right here.
And you can do some really interesting things with these.
And that's a quick walkthrough of Muse.
We're really excited for you to check it out.
You can download Muse today.
